_note: Friendly editorial copy grounded in this group's personas.json. These are jokes, not attributed quotes. Pick-specific copy requires the matching team and direction.

default: Matt needs {team} to make this pick look good. If it does not, expect a description featuring untapped potential, strong fundamentals, and a motivated seller.
If {team} lets Matt down, the group should watch for the phrase priced to move. Every pick is a listing if you believe in yourself.
Matt can sell a property. Selling the group on {team} after a bad Saturday may take a second open house.

Penn State|O: Matt is selling the Penn State Over. A bad Saturday would be an excellent time for the group to ask whether the listing price has been reduced.
Texas Tech|U: Matt took the Texas Tech Under. He sells real estate, so the group is entitled to ask for the comps before he declares this program overpriced.

default: Hauck hosts the game and keeps the receipts. If {team} cooperates, expect documentation. If it does not, hosting duties may suddenly become very absorbing.
If {team} cooperates, Hauck's receipts get another page. The group should establish a reasonable limit on the presentation length.
Hauck tastes wine seriously. If {team} spoils the weekend, expect questions about the finish.

Kentucky|O: Hauck is an Ohio State man with a Kentucky Over. The group should ask whether this is a serious investment or just a tasting flight of SEC football.
Ohio State|O: Hauck wants Ohio State wins. No tasting notes, no complicated explanation: this is the house pour.

default: Bryan runs a PE group and tends ferns. Now he needs growth from {team}. The group can ask whether this pick requires more patience, more capital, or a sunnier window.
If {team} needs more time, Bryan can call it a long-term investment. The group can ask whether the ferns are outperforming it.
Bryan is accustomed to taking Zach's poker money. This {team} pick requires cooperation from people who were not invited to poker night.

South Florida|O: Bryan needs South Florida wins. A PE guy buying into the Bulls: the branding practically wrote the investment memo for him.

default: Todd has decades of Browns practice at accepting outcomes. If {team} makes this difficult, the group can test whether that famously unbothered calm covers college football too.
Todd drives a Rivian. If {team} stalls, the group can ask whether the problem is range anxiety or just college football.
If {team} ruins the mood, Todd still has Atlas to walk. That is a very large alternative to reading the group chat.

South Florida|U: Todd needs South Florida losses. The calmest man in the room has volunteered for a season of watching someone else's offense and hoping it stalls. Very Browns-adjacent relaxation.

default: Zach's poker money has a habit of leaving with someone else. Now he needs {team} to prove that building a second game was a sound recovery strategy.
If {team} helps Zach win, he can finally describe a game night without explaining where his money went.
Zach built the website. {team} has so far declined to accept bug reports about its results.

LSU|O: Zach took the LSU Over. The group may ask how many lines of code were necessary to reach the same conclusion as his LSU shirt.

default: Josh bought a VR treadmill to move through imaginary worlds. This weekend, {team} has to make actual progress. The group should clarify which kind is showing up in the standings.
Josh can walk through virtual worlds. If {team} lets him down, the group should ask whether a more agreeable season is available in VR.
If {team} makes this pick look good, Josh can enjoy the result sitting down. The treadmill does not need to be involved in everything.

Stanford|O: Josh works at a vineyard and took the Stanford Over. If it needs time to develop, the group should ask whether this is a football pick or something he is aging in a barrel.

default: Mark sells bread for a living. He needs {team} to make this pick rise. If it falls flat, the group has a regrettably large supply of bakery jokes ready.
Mark works in bread. If {team} cooperates, the group can concede that he knows which side this pick is buttered on.
If {team} struggles, Mark may hear the word toast more than he would like. Occupational hazards now include the group chat.

Indiana|O: Mark went to Indiana and took the Indiana Over. The diploma explains the loyalty; the scoreboard still has to explain the pick.
